metadata.title: Real Estate ERP Platform Data Assets
metadata.description: Catalog of the portfolio, relation, letting, contract, rent, bank, ledger, maintenance, owners'-association, analytics, portal, automation and tenant data assets that power the real estate lifecycle (Portfolio, Let, Contract, Collect, Maintain, Account, Report, Serve) on the combined Bloxs + Informant ERP platform, with classification, GDPR/AVG and Dutch fiscal, tenancy, banking and building-regulation governance, backing stores, and team ownership.

rootGroups.name: Portfolio and Relations Data
rootGroups.description: What the real estate organisation owns or manages and who it deals with: legal entities, objects, complexes and rental units, valuations and market data, development project budgets, the single relation database of tenants, owners, investors and suppliers, and the documents and correspondence attached to all of them. Objects carry almost no personal data but are the spine every contract, invoice and ticket hangs from; relations are where GDPR/AVG obligations begin.

subGroups.name: Objects, Entities and Projects
subGroups.description: The portfolio master data and its valuation and project layers: owning entities, buildings and units, appraisal and WOZ values, and development or transformation project budgets.

assets.name: Property Object
assets.description: A building, complex, parcel or portfolio node of a tenant organisation: address and BAG identifiers, Kadaster parcel and apartment-right references, object type (residential, commercial, retail, logistics, healthcare, parking, land), year of construction, gross and lettable floor area, energy label and EP-online registration, owning legal entity and acquisition data, split ownership and VvE membership, insurance and tax attributes, photos and floor plans, and the hierarchy from portfolio to complex to building. Maintained in Objects, Complexes and Units (objt), valued by Valuations and Market Data (valu), extended by Development and Transformation Projects (proj), inspected through Installations and Periodic Maintenance (inst), imported by Data Migration and Onboarding Tooling (migr) and aggregated in Dashboards and Data Analytics (dash).
assets.businessMeaning: The physical asset the whole business exists to exploit: every unit, contract, invoice, ticket and valuation resolves to one object, and portfolio value and yield are reported per object.
assets.accessScope: portfolio, asset management, technical and finance staff of the owning tenant organisation; owner clients see their own objects through the owner portal; descriptive attributes of vacant units published through listings

interfaces.name: property-object api
interfaces.description: CRUD, hierarchy, and lookup API for portfolios, complexes and buildings with BAG and Kadaster reference resolution, used by the back-office objects module, valuations, projects, technical management, portals, migration tooling and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: object lifecycle events
interfaces.description: Object acquired, attributes changed, energy label updated, ownership transferred, and object sold or demolished events consumed by valuations, contracts, the ledger, dashboards and integration webhooks.

governance.retention: kept for the life of the object in the portfolio; after sale or demolition kept 10 years because the Belastingdienst requires immovable-property data (VAT revision period) to be retained 10 years instead of the general 7
governance.sharingPolicy: owned by the tenant organisation; object facts shared with its owner clients, appraisers, insurers and maintenance partners per object; published attributes of vacant units public in listings; never shared between tenant organisations; anonymised object-type facts may feed cross-tenant benchmarks

assets.name: Rental Unit
assets.description: An individually lettable unit within a property object: apartment, house, office floor, shop, warehouse bay, parking place or storage: unit number and BAG address, unit type and use, floor area, rooms, amenities, energy label, woningwaarderingsstelsel (WWS) points and maximum regulated rent under the Wet betaalbare huur, market rent estimate, target rent, current letting status (let, vacant, notice given, under renovation, not for let), meters and keys, and the chain of current and historical lease contracts. Maintained in Objects, Complexes and Units (objt), listed by Vacancy, Letting and Candidate Screening (vacm) and referenced by every fault report in Fault Reports and Tickets (tick).
assets.businessMeaning: The unit of occupancy and revenue: occupancy rate, vacancy days and rent per square metre are all counted per rental unit, and Dutch rent regulation is applied per unit.
assets.accessScope: portfolio, letting, technical and finance staff of the owning tenant organisation; the sitting tenant sees its own unit in the tenant portal; the owner client sees its own units; vacant-unit attributes public in listings

interfaces.name: rental-unit api
interfaces.description: Unit maintenance, letting-status, WWS points and rent-ceiling lookup API used by the objects module, vacancy and letting, contracts, rent invoicing, tickets, the tenant and owner portals and the Huurprijscheck.app rent-price check connector.

interfaces.name: unit status events
interfaces.description: Unit created, vacant, listed, let, notice given and renovation started or completed events consumed by vacancy listings, rent runs, occupancy dashboards and maintenance planning.

governance.retention: kept for the life of the unit; WWS point calculations and rent-ceiling history kept 7 years after the unit's last lease ended so that historical rents can be substantiated to the Huurcommissie and in rent-increase disputes
governance.sharingPolicy: owned by the tenant organisation; unit facts shared with the sitting tenant, the owner client and maintenance partners per unit; listed vacant units public; never shared between tenant organisations

assets.name: Legal Entity
assets.description: An owning, managing or contracting legal person administered by a tenant organisation: investment B.V., C.V. or fund, owner client company, private owner acting as landlord, or an owners' association (VvE) as a legal person: KvK number, VAT number and VAT position (VAT-opted commercial lets), fiscal unity and group structure, bank accounts and mandates, directors and UBO records, accounting settings (chart of accounts, RGS mapping, fiscal year, cost centres), reporting currency and consolidation membership. Maintained in Objects, Complexes and Units (objt) as the owner of objects, used by Multi-Entity General Ledger and Period Close (ledg) as the bookkeeping entity, and by Association Budgets, Contributions and Reserve Funds (vveb) for each association's own books.
assets.businessMeaning: The bookkeeping and contracting boundary of multi-entity real estate: every object is owned by an entity, every invoice is issued by one, and investor and owner reporting is consolidated across them.
assets.accessScope: finance and portfolio management staff of the owning tenant organisation with entity-level roles; owner clients see their own entities in the owner portal; bank account changes under four-eyes approval

interfaces.name: legal-entity api
interfaces.description: Entity, ownership structure, fiscal setting and bank mandate API used by the objects module, the multi-entity ledger, rent invoicing (issuing entity), VvE administration, investor reporting and accounting connectors.

interfaces.name: entity lifecycle events
interfaces.description: Entity created, ownership changed, fiscal setting changed, bank account changed (four-eyes approved) and entity liquidated events consumed by the ledger, rent runs, consolidation and integration routing.

governance.retention: kept while the entity is administered plus 7 years after its last fiscal year under Dutch fiscal retention; UBO and identification records kept 5 years after the end of the business relationship where Wwft customer due diligence applies
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the tenant organisation; entity data shared with its accountant, auditor, banks and the tenant's accounting or consolidation package; directors' and UBO personal data limited to compliance roles; never shared between tenant organisations

assets.name: Valuation Record
assets.description: A dated value of a property object or unit with its basis: external appraisal by an NRVT-registered valuer (market value, investment value, rebuild value for insurance) with the report document, WOZ decision value and objection status, internal desktop valuation, IFRS or Dutch GAAP (RJ) fair value used in the annual accounts, gross and net initial yield, market rent and reference transactions, and imported market data series. Maintained in Valuations and Market Data (valu) on top of the object register, consumed by Dashboards and Data Analytics (dash), Investor and Owner Reporting (ivrp) and the ledger's revaluation postings.
assets.businessMeaning: What the portfolio is worth and why: the basis for investor NAV, lender covenants, insurance sums, WOZ-based taxes and hold/sell decisions.
assets.accessScope: asset managers, finance and directors of the owning tenant organisation; owner clients see valuations of their own objects in the owner portal; valuers upload reports through documents; never visible to tenants or suppliers

interfaces.name: valuation api
interfaces.description: Record, version, approve and query API for valuations and market data series with yield and value-per-square-metre calculations, used by the valuations module, dashboards, investor reporting, ledger revaluations and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: market data and WOZ imports
interfaces.description: Scheduled import of WOZ decision values, CBS and market index series, and appraiser valuation exports matched to objects by BAG identifier.

interfaces.name: valuation events
interfaces.description: Valuation recorded, approved, WOZ objection filed and value materially changed events consumed by dashboards, investor reporting and workflow alerts on covenant thresholds.

governance.retention: every valuation version kept 7 years after the fiscal year it supported in the annual accounts; valuations of sold objects follow the 10-year immovable-property retention of the object
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the tenant organisation; shared with its owner clients, auditors, lenders and investors through reporting; appraisal reports never shared between tenant organisations; only anonymised value and yield facts feed benchmarks

assets.name: Project Budget
assets.description: The financial model of a new-build, renovation or transformation project on one or more objects: budget lines per cost category (land, construction, installations, fees, financing, contingency), commitments and contracts with contractors, change orders, invoiced and paid amounts, forecast to complete, VAT treatment (new-build VAT, transfer tax, VAT revision on immovable property), milestones and hand-over into exploitation, and linked documents and drawings. Maintained in Development and Transformation Projects (proj), fed by Accounts Payable and Supplier Invoices (payb) and posted through Multi-Entity General Ledger and Period Close (ledg).
assets.businessMeaning: Whether a transformation creates or destroys value: budget versus commitment versus actual per project decides capital calls, lender draws and the exploitation start.
assets.accessScope: project managers, asset managers and finance staff of the owning tenant organisation; owner and investor clients see summary progress in reporting; contractors see only their own commitments through the supplier portal

interfaces.name: project-budget api
interfaces.description: Budget, commitment, change-order, forecast and milestone API with budget-versus-actual queries, used by the projects module, supplier-invoice coding, ledger postings, dashboards and investor reporting.

interfaces.name: project financial events
interfaces.description: Budget approved, commitment added, budget overrun flagged, milestone reached and project handed over events consumed by workflow approvals, ledger capitalisation and portfolio dashboards.

governance.retention: project lifetime plus 10 years because project costs capitalised into immovable property fall under the Belastingdienst 10-year retention for VAT revision; approved budget versions immutable
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the tenant organisation; shared with its investors, lenders and auditors through reporting; contractor-specific commitments shared only with that contractor; never shared between tenant organisations

subGroups.name: Relations and Documents
subGroups.description: One relation database for every counterparty of the organisation and the documents and correspondence attached to relations, objects, contracts and cases.

assets.name: Contact Relation
assets.description: The CRM record of a person or organisation a tenant organisation deals with: tenant (private or business), rental candidate, owner client, investor, apartment owner in a VvE, supplier or contractor, broker, notary, accountant or municipality: relation roles, contact details and communication preferences, correspondence language, bank details and SEPA mandates, identification status, linked objects, units, contracts and cases, e-mail and telephone threads synchronised from Gmail and Outlook, and notes. Maintained in Relations and CRM (rela), enriched by Documents and Correspondence (docm), contracted through Lease Contracts and E-Signing (cntr), reminded by Debtor Management and Dunning (dunn) and served through Meetings, Decisions and Owner Communication (vvem).
assets.businessMeaning: Who the organisation has obligations to and claims on: one relation record per person or company avoids the double tenants, wrong addresses and mismatched bank accounts that legacy spreadsheets produced.
assets.accessScope: letting, finance, technical and VvE staff of the owning tenant organisation by role; each relation manages its own contact data through its portal; AI assistants read through the tenant organisation's own permissions

interfaces.name: contact-relation api
interfaces.description: Search, create, merge, update and consent-aware read API for relations and their roles, used by the back office, letting, contracts, invoicing, dunning, all portals, the Gmail and Outlook connectors, AI assistants and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: relation events
interfaces.description: Relation created, merged, role added, contact or bank details changed (four-eyes for bank changes), consent changed and erasure requested events consumed by contracts, rent runs, portals and data-subject-request workflows.

governance.retention: kept 7 years after the last contract, invoice or contribution because the relation anchors fiscal records; candidates without a contract deleted per the candidate-application retention; suppliers without invoices deleted 2 years after last contact; erasure requests honoured except for data locked by fiscal retention
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the tenant organisation; contact data shared with maintenance partners only for access to a unit, with the e-mail provider under the user's own mailbox, and with accounting packages as debtor or creditor data; never shared between tenant organisations

assets.name: Document Record
assets.description: A stored document or piece of correspondence with its metadata and links: signed lease contracts and addenda with e-signature evidence, deeds and Kadaster extracts, energy labels, inspection and appraisal reports, invoices and settlement statements, generated letters (indexation, dunning, termination confirmations), owner statements, VvE meeting notices and minutes, drawings and photos, and e-mails threaded from Gmail and Outlook: document type, related object, unit, relation, contract or case, version, template used, generation source, sender and recipients, signature status and retention class. Managed in Documents and Correspondence (docm), generated by Lease Contracts and E-Signing (cntr), drafted or classified by AI Assistants (aiag) and exposed in the Owner Portal (ownp) and other portals.
assets.businessMeaning: The paper trail of real estate management: what was agreed, sent and signed with whom, retrievable from the object, the relation or the contract in seconds instead of from a filing cabinet.
assets.accessScope: staff of the owning tenant organisation by document class and role; each tenant, owner or supplier downloads documents addressed to it through its portal; AI assistants access documents through the tenant organisation's permissions

interfaces.name: document api
interfaces.description: Upload, generate-from-template, version, classify, secure-download and retention-class API for documents, used by every back-office module, the e-signing connector, the Gmail and Outlook connectors, AI assistants, all portals and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: document events
interfaces.description: Document uploaded, generated, sent, signed, viewed in portal and retention expired events consumed by workflow tasks, portal notifications, contract status and self-service KPIs.

governance.retention: per retention class: contracts, invoices and statements 7 years after the fiscal year in which the underlying contract ended; deeds and building documents for the life of the object plus 10 years; candidate documents per the candidate-application rule; other correspondence 2 years after the related case closed
governance.sharingPolicy: shared only with the relations a document is addressed to or signed by, through their portals or expiring links; signed contracts shared with the e-signing provider under a processor agreement; never shared between tenant organisations

rootGroups.name: Letting and Contract Data
rootGroups.description: The let and contract stages: vacancy listings, candidate applications with their screening data, the lease contract that becomes the legal source of every rent and service-charge obligation, and the annual service charge settlement. Candidate and tenant personal data enters here under the Dutch good-landlordship and affordable-rent rules, and the fiscal trail of the lease begins.

subGroups.name: Letting and Screening
subGroups.description: From vacant unit to selected candidate: listings, applications and the compliance checks around them.

assets.name: Vacancy Listing
assets.description: A published or planned advertisement of a vacant rental unit: asking rent and service charge advance, WWS points and regulated maximum rent where applicable, energy label, availability date, minimum lease term, income and guarantee requirements, the transparent selection procedure and selection criteria required by the Wet goed verhuurderschap, viewing slots, photos and texts, publication channels (own website, listing portals, brokers) and the response and viewing statistics. Created in Vacancy, Letting and Candidate Screening (vacm) from the rental unit, rent-checked through the Huurprijscheck.app connector and closed when a lease is signed in Lease Contracts and E-Signing (cntr).
assets.businessMeaning: The instrument that turns vacancy days into a signed lease: the listing's rent, criteria and selection procedure are also the landlord's evidence of a fair and compliant letting.
assets.accessScope: letting staff of the owning tenant organisation; owner clients approve listings for their units through the owner portal; published attributes public on listing channels

interfaces.name: vacancy-listing api
interfaces.description: Create, rent-check, publish, schedule viewings and close API for listings, used by the letting module, the owner portal approval flow, listing-portal feeds, the rent-price check connector and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: listing lifecycle events
interfaces.description: Listing published, viewing booked, application received, listing closed and days-vacant threshold events consumed by workflow tasks, occupancy dashboards and owner notifications.

governance.retention: closed listings kept 7 years as evidence of the selection procedure, rent offered and WWS calculation under the good-landlordship and affordable-rent rules; response statistics anonymised after 24 months
governance.sharingPolicy: published attributes public on the tenant organisation's own site and listing partners; selection criteria disclosed to candidates; owner clients see listings of their own units; never shared between tenant organisations

assets.name: Candidate Application
assets.description: A prospective tenant's application for a listed unit: applicant and co-applicants, household composition, contact details, employment and income evidence (payslips, employer statement, annual statement), landlord reference, identification status with BSN and photo masked as the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens requires, guarantor details, screening outcome against the published criteria with the reasons recorded for the mandatory rejection notice, viewing attendance, ranking and allocation decision, and for commercial leases the Wwft identification and UBO checks where the rent exceeds the intermediation threshold. Captured through the tenant portal or brokers in Vacancy, Letting and Candidate Screening (vacm) and, when selected, converted into a relation and a lease in Lease Contracts and E-Signing (cntr).
assets.businessMeaning: The compliance-critical moment of letting: selecting the right tenant fast while being able to prove a non-discriminatory, transparent procedure and holding no more candidate data than the law allows.
assets.accessScope: letting staff of the owning tenant organisation with a screening role; the candidate sees and edits its own application through the portal; owner clients see only the anonymised ranking and the selected candidate's summary; brokers see applications they submitted

interfaces.name: candidate-application api
interfaces.description: Apply, upload evidence, screen, rank, allocate, reject-with-reason and purge API for applications with field-level masking, used by the letting module, the tenant portal application flow, broker submissions and the rejection-letter template.

interfaces.name: application events
interfaces.description: Application received, evidence complete, screened, allocated, rejected and purged events consumed by workflow tasks, listing statistics and the contract creation flow.

governance.retention: data of non-selected candidates deleted 4 weeks after the unit is allocated unless the candidate consented to be kept for later vacancies (maximum 1 year); the selected candidate's income evidence deleted after contract signature except the summary the lease relies on; Wwft identification records for commercial leases kept 5 years; ID copies never stored unmasked; screening decisions logged for the good-landlordship evidence duty
governance.sharingPolicy: never shared beyond the letting staff of the tenant organisation and the candidate itself; owner clients receive only the selection outcome; identity-verification providers process data under a processor agreement; never used for marketing; never shared between tenant organisations

subGroups.name: Lease Contracts and Settlements
subGroups.description: The legal core of the tenancy: the lease contract with its rent, indexation and terms, and the annual service charge settlement derived from it.

assets.name: Lease Contract
assets.description: The tenancy agreement between a landlord entity and one or more tenants for a rental unit: contract type (residential regulated or liberalised, ROZ commercial office or retail, parking, storage), start date, fixed or indefinite term, notice periods and break options, rent components (net rent, service charge advance, VAT status of an opted commercial let), indexation clause (CPI, ministerial maximum increase for regulated and mid-rent segments) and indexation history, deposit or bank guarantee (capped at two months' rent under the Wet goed verhuurderschap), special terms and addenda, co-tenants and guarantors, SEPA direct-debit mandate reference, termination and settlement status, and the signed document with its eIDAS e-signature evidence package. Captured once in Lease Contracts and E-Signing (cntr), changed over time by Rent Indexation, Renewals and Terminations (indx), settled by Service Charges and Settlements (svcc) and billed by Rent Invoicing and Billing Runs (rent).
assets.businessMeaning: The single legal source of every rent euro: all invoices, indexations, settlements and terminations derive from the contract, and rent regulation is applied to it.
assets.accessScope: letting, contract and finance staff of the owning tenant organisation; the tenant sees and downloads its own contract in the tenant portal; the owner client sees contracts on its own units; read-only for BI

interfaces.name: lease-contract api
interfaces.description: Create, generate document, send for e-signature, activate, index, amend, renew, terminate and query API for contracts and their rent components, used by the contracts module, indexation robots, service charge settlement, rent runs, tenant and owner portals, the e-signing connector and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: contract lifecycle events
interfaces.description: Contract drafted, signed, activated, indexed, amended, notice given, terminated and deposit settled events consumed by rent invoicing, service charges, occupancy dashboards, workflow tasks and integration webhooks.

governance.retention: 7 years after the fiscal year in which the contract ended under Dutch fiscal retention because it substantiates rent invoices; the signed document and e-signature evidence retained immutably for the same period; deposit settlement records kept with the contract
governance.sharingPolicy: shared with the tenant party and the owner client of the unit; signature evidence exchanged with the e-signing provider; contract rent data shared with the tenant organisation's accountant and auditor; never shared between tenant organisations

assets.name: Service Charge Settlement
assets.description: The annual (or final, on termination) settlement of service charges and utility costs for a complex and its contracts: cost pools per complex (cleaning, caretaker, lifts, communal energy, heat under the Warmtewet, water, insurance, VvE contribution pass-through), allocation keys per unit and contract (floor area, units, occupancy days, meter readings), advances invoiced during the year, the settled amount per tenant, the settlement statement with specification, dispute status with the Huurcommissie for regulated units, and the resulting invoices or credit notes. Calculated in Service Charges and Settlements (svcc) from the lease contract and supplier invoices, and billed through Rent Invoicing and Billing Runs (rent).
assets.businessMeaning: The most error-prone yearly obligation of a landlord: the settlement must be issued within the legal term, be specified per cost category and survive a Huurcommissie review, and it decides whether the organisation recovers its service costs.
assets.accessScope: contract and finance staff of the owning tenant organisation; each tenant sees its own settlement statement in the tenant portal; owner clients see settlements of their complexes

interfaces.name: service-charge settlement api
interfaces.description: Cost pool, allocation key, meter reading, calculate, approve, issue statement and dispute API used by the service charge module, rent invoicing, the tenant and owner portals and settlement robots.

interfaces.name: settlement events
interfaces.description: Settlement calculated, approved, statements issued, dispute opened and settlement term approaching events consumed by rent invoicing, workflow deadlines, tenant notifications and recovery dashboards.

governance.retention: 7 years after the fiscal year of the settlement under Dutch fiscal retention; underlying meter readings and allocation keys kept with the settlement because tenants may bring a regulated-rent settlement to the Huurcommissie up to 24 months after the settlement term
governance.sharingPolicy: each tenant receives only its own statement and the complex-level specification it is entitled to; owner clients and auditors see complex settlements; never shared between tenant organisations

rootGroups.name: Finance and Accounting Data
rootGroups.description: The collect and account stages: periodic rent invoices and the payments that clear them, bank statement lines ingested through PSD2 and CAMT files, the multi-entity general ledger, and supplier invoices. Everything here is a fiscal record under the Belastingdienst 7-year (10-year for immovable property) retention and the basis of every investor and owner statement.

subGroups.name: Rent and Collection
subGroups.description: Money in: rent invoices produced by billing runs, the payments and direct debits against them, and the bank statement lines they are reconciled with.

assets.name: Rent Invoice
assets.description: An invoice, credit note or contribution request issued to a tenant, apartment owner or other debtor by a landlord or association entity: invoice number in the entity's fiscal sequence, period, lines for net rent, service charge advance, heat and utilities, VAT on opted commercial lets, indexation corrections and settlement amounts, due date and payment method (SEPA direct debit with mandate reference and pre-notification, iDEAL payment link, bank transfer), dunning stage and interest, and the PDF and UBL e-invoice renditions. Produced by Rent Invoicing and Billing Runs (rent), adjusted by Rent Indexation, Renewals and Terminations (indx), reported by VAT and Tax Handling (vatx), chased by Debtor Management and Dunning (dunn) and shown in the Tenant Portal and App (tenp).
assets.businessMeaning: The claim on the tenant and the revenue record of the unit: the amount the landlord books as rental income, reports for VAT and reports to investors, and the line every bank receipt must be matched against.
assets.accessScope: finance and debtor staff of the owning tenant organisation; each tenant or owner sees its own invoices in its portal; read-only access for BI and auditors

interfaces.name: rent-invoice api
interfaces.description: Billing-run, issue, credit, render, direct-debit batch and query API for invoices, used by the rent module, indexation, service charge settlement, VvE contributions, dunning, tenant and owner portals, VAT returns, accounting export and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: SEPA direct debit and e-invoice exchange
interfaces.description: Generation of SEPA direct debit (pain.008) batches per entity bank account with pre-notifications, and UBL e-invoice delivery to business tenants.

interfaces.name: invoice lifecycle events
interfaces.description: Billing run completed, invoice issued, direct debit collected or reversed, due, overdue, paid and credited events consumed by bank reconciliation, dunning, workflow tasks, portals and rent-collection dashboards.

governance.retention: 7 years after the fiscal year of issue under Dutch fiscal retention; immutable once issued, corrections only by credit note; direct-debit mandate references kept 14 months after the last collection as SEPA evidence
governance.sharingPolicy: shared with the invoiced tenant or owner, the tenant organisation's accountant, auditor and accounting package, and the Belastingdienst via VAT returns and audit files; never shared between tenant organisations

assets.name: Payment Transaction
assets.description: A money movement matched to one or more rent invoices, contributions or supplier invoices of an entity: SEPA direct debit collection or reversal (R-transaction with reason code), iDEAL or card payment through the payment link in the tenant portal, incoming bank transfer, refund of a deposit or settlement credit, supplier payment run, and the matching state (auto-matched by the reconciliation robot, manually matched, unallocated, partially paid) with the matching rule applied. Recorded by Bank Integration and Reconciliation (bank) from bank statement lines and payment-provider webhooks, consumed by Debtor Management and Dunning (dunn) to stop or escalate reminders and shown in the Tenant Portal and App (tenp) as paid and outstanding amounts.
assets.businessMeaning: Whether the rent actually arrived: the trigger for stopping dunning, releasing deposits and closing the debtor position, and the cash side of every period close.
assets.accessScope: finance staff of the owning tenant organisation; tenants and owners see their own payment status; payment-provider references only, no card data held

interfaces.name: payment api
interfaces.description: Create payment link, record payment, match, unmatch, refund and payment-run API used by the bank module, dunning, the tenant portal checkout, supplier payment runs and accounting export.

interfaces.name: payment status events
interfaces.description: Payment received, direct debit reversed, matched, unallocated, refunded and payment run executed events consumed by dunning, deposit settlement, portals, period close and cash dashboards.

governance.retention: 7 years after the fiscal year of the transaction under Dutch fiscal retention; payment-provider references kept, card details held only by the provider
governance.sharingPolicy: exchanged with the entity's bank, the PSD2 account-information provider, the payment service provider and the tenant organisation's accounting package; payment status shared with the paying tenant or owner; never shared between tenant organisations

assets.name: Bank Statement Line
assets.description: A single booked transaction on a bank account of a landlord, management or association entity, ingested daily from the bank: statement and entry reference, booking and value date, amount and currency, counterparty name and IBAN, remittance information and end-to-end identifiers, SEPA transaction code, and the ingestion source (PSD2 account-information API through a licensed provider under a consent renewed every 180 days, CAMT.053 or MT940 file, or manual upload) with duplicate detection. Ingested by Bank Integration and Reconciliation (bank), which matches lines to rent invoices, contributions and supplier invoices into payment transactions and posts the remainder as bank mutations to Multi-Entity General Ledger and Period Close (ledg).
assets.businessMeaning: The raw truth of the bank: every line must end up matched or explained, and the automated matching rate is the difference between daily and month-end reconciliation.
assets.accessScope: finance staff of the owning tenant organisation with bank roles per entity account; reconciliation robots read and match; never visible to tenants, owners or suppliers

interfaces.name: bank statement ingestion
interfaces.description: Daily intake of CAMT.053 and MT940 statement files per entity bank account with duplicate and gap detection, plus manual upload for banks without connectivity.

interfaces.name: bank account-information and matching api
interfaces.description: PSD2 account-information pull through the licensed bank connector, consent status, and line matching, splitting and posting API used by the bank module, reconciliation robots and the ledger.

interfaces.name: bank line events
interfaces.description: Statement received, line matched, line unmatched, consent expiring and statement gap detected events consumed by reconciliation dashboards, workflow tasks and the period-close checklist.

governance.retention: 7 years after the fiscal year of the statement under Dutch fiscal retention; original statement files retained immutably in the landing zone; counterparty personal data kept as part of the fiscal record
governance.sharingPolicy: obtained from the entity's bank under PSD2 consent or file exchange; shared with the tenant organisation's accountant and auditor; never shared with tenants, suppliers or other tenant organisations

subGroups.name: Real Estate Accounting
subGroups.description: The books: general ledger entries per entity with period close and consolidation, and the supplier invoices that flow into them.

assets.name: General Ledger Entry
assets.description: A posting line in the books of a landlord, management or association entity: journal, date and period, account in the entity's chart of accounts with RGS mapping, cost centre and object or unit dimension, debit and credit amount, VAT code and return box, counter-entry, source document (rent invoice, supplier invoice, bank line, settlement, revaluation, depreciation, intercompany, manual journal), posting user or robot, period-close and consolidation state, and audit trail. Maintained by Multi-Entity General Ledger and Period Close (ledg), fed by Accounts Payable and Supplier Invoices (payb), reported by VAT and Tax Handling (vatx) and consumed by Investor and Owner Reporting (ivrp).
assets.businessMeaning: The legally required books of every entity: the source of VAT returns, annual accounts, investor NAV and owner statements, and the record the Belastingdienst may audit.
assets.accessScope: accounting staff of the owning tenant organisation with entity-level roles; owner and investor clients see derived statements only; auditors and the tax authority receive audit files on request

interfaces.name: general-ledger api
interfaces.description: Post, reverse, query, trial balance, period close, VAT return and consolidation API used by the ledger module, all posting modules, VAT handling, investor reporting, accounting connectors and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: audit file and accounting exchange
interfaces.description: XML Audit File (XAF) export for the Belastingdienst and auditors, and journal exchange with external accounting or consolidation packages through certified connectors.

interfaces.name: ledger events
interfaces.description: Entry posted, period closed, period reopened, VAT return filed and consolidation completed events consumed by dashboards, investor reporting, workflow checklists and integration webhooks.

governance.retention: 7 years after the fiscal year under Dutch fiscal retention (art. 52 AWR and 2:10 BW); postings on immovable property kept 10 years for the VAT revision period; closed periods immutable, corrections only in open periods
governance.sharingPolicy: shared with the entity's accountant, auditor, the Belastingdienst on request and the tenant organisation's accounting or consolidation package; derived statements shared with owners and investors; never shared between tenant organisations

assets.name: Supplier Invoice
assets.description: An incoming invoice or credit note from a maintenance supplier, contractor, utility, insurer, municipality or service provider, received by e-mail, supplier-portal upload, Peppol or UBL e-invoice, or scan: supplier and invoice number, date and currency, lines coded to entity, object, unit, cost category, project budget or service charge cost pool, VAT treatment including reverse-charged construction VAT, matching against the work order or project commitment, discrepancy flags, approval workflow state with owner-client approval where the management mandate requires it, chain-liability (WKA) blocked-account split for subcontractors, payment run assignment and the accounts-payable posting. Managed by Accounts Payable and Supplier Invoices (payb), matched by Work Orders and Supplier Dispatch (work), coded by AI Assistants (aiag) and paid through Bank Integration and Reconciliation (bank).
assets.businessMeaning: What the organisation actually owes for maintenance and services versus what was ordered: three-way matching here decides whether costs are recoverable through service charges, chargeable to owners or lost.
assets.accessScope: finance and technical staff of the owning tenant organisation with approval roles; owner clients approve invoices above their mandate through the owner portal; suppliers see their own invoice status through the supplier portal

interfaces.name: supplier-invoice api
interfaces.description: Register, recognise, code, match, approve, dispute and schedule-for-payment API used by the accounts payable module, supplier portal upload, invoice-recognition assistants, owner approvals and accounting export.

interfaces.name: e-invoice and accounting exchange
interfaces.description: Intake of Peppol and UBL e-invoices and e-mailed PDFs, and export of approved purchase invoices and payment runs to external accounting packages through certified connectors.

interfaces.name: supplier invoice events
interfaces.description: Invoice received, coded, matched, discrepancy flagged, approved, paid and disputed events consumed by workflow approvals, service charge cost pools, project budgets and supplier payment-time dashboards.

governance.retention: 7 years after the fiscal year of receipt under Dutch fiscal retention, 10 years where the invoice concerns immovable property; original invoice images retained immutably
governance.sharingPolicy: shared with the tenant organisation's accountant, auditor and accounting package; status shared with the issuing supplier; cost lines shared with owner clients and, through settlements, with tenants; never shared between tenant organisations

rootGroups.name: Technical Management Data
rootGroups.description: The maintain stage: fault reports from tenants and owners, the work orders dispatched to suppliers, the register of installations with their inspection obligations, and multi-year maintenance plans and budgets. Tickets and work orders carry tenant contact and access data; installations and plans carry building-regulation obligations rather than personal data.

subGroups.name: Maintenance Operations
subGroups.description: From fault report to completed work: tickets and the work orders that resolve them.

assets.name: Maintenance Ticket
assets.description: A fault report or maintenance request on a unit, complex or installation: reporter (tenant through the portal or app, owner, caretaker, inspection), category and urgency (leak, heating failure, lift, lock-out, mould), description and photos, affected unit and installation, access arrangements and contact preferences, responsibility assessment (landlord repair duty versus tenant minor repairs under the Besluit kleine herstellingen), triage decision, linked work orders, status timeline, resolution and the tenant's satisfaction rating. Managed in Fault Reports and Tickets (tick), triaged by AI Assistants (aiag) and maintenance-partner connectors, executed through Work Orders and Supplier Dispatch (work) and followed in the Tenant Portal and App (tenp).
assets.businessMeaning: The moment the tenant judges the landlord: response and resolution time per ticket drive tenant satisfaction, legal repair-duty compliance and the workload of the technical team.
assets.accessScope: technical staff of the owning tenant organisation; the reporting tenant follows its own ticket in the portal; owner clients see tickets on their own units; the dispatched supplier sees the ticket details needed for the job

interfaces.name: maintenance-ticket api
interfaces.description: Report, attach photos, triage, assign, update status, close and rate API for tickets, used by the technical module, tenant portal and app, owner portal, AI triage, Ziezodan and Proprli connectors and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: ticket lifecycle events
interfaces.description: Ticket reported, triaged, work order created, resolved, closed and response-time breached events consumed by work orders, tenant notifications, workflow escalations and resolution-time dashboards.

governance.retention: closed tickets kept 5 years for repair-duty and liability evidence; photos of the interior of a home deleted 2 years after closure; reporter contact details minimised to the relation record
governance.sharingPolicy: shared with the reporting tenant, the owner client of the unit and the dispatched supplier limited to the job; exchanged with maintenance-partner platforms under processor agreements; never shared between tenant organisations

assets.name: Work Order
assets.description: An instruction to a supplier or in-house technician to perform work on a unit, complex or installation: originating ticket or maintenance plan item, scope and instructions, object and unit with access details and tenant contact window, supplier and required certification, quote request and accepted quote, budget or price agreement, cost allocation (owner, landlord, tenant recharge, service charge pool, project), planned date and visit slots, execution status (sent, accepted, planned, executed, completed, verified), completion report with photos, and the matched supplier invoice. Managed in Work Orders and Supplier Dispatch (work), created from Fault Reports and Tickets (tick) and Installations and Periodic Maintenance (inst), accepted and reported through the Supplier and Partner Portal (sprp) and matched in Accounts Payable and Supplier Invoices (payb).
assets.businessMeaning: The commitment to spend and the proof of execution: the work order is what the supplier is paid against and what tells the owner what was done to their property and why.
assets.accessScope: technical and finance staff of the owning tenant organisation; the assigned supplier sees and updates its own work orders in the supplier portal; owner clients approve work above their mandate; tenants see the planned visit for their unit

interfaces.name: work-order api
interfaces.description: Create, request quote, dispatch, accept, plan, report completion, verify and cost-allocate API for work orders, used by the technical module, supplier portal, owner approvals, maintenance-partner connectors, invoice matching and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: work order events
interfaces.description: Work order sent, accepted, declined, planned, completed, verified and overdue events consumed by ticket status, tenant and owner notifications, workflow escalations, invoice matching and turnaround dashboards.

governance.retention: 7 years after the fiscal year of the matched supplier invoice under Dutch fiscal retention because the work order substantiates the cost; access details and tenant contact windows removed 90 days after completion
governance.sharingPolicy: shared with the assigned supplier limited to the job and access details, with the owner client for approval and statements, and with the tenant for visit planning; exchanged with maintenance-partner platforms under processor agreements; never shared between tenant organisations

subGroups.name: Installations and Planning
subGroups.description: The technical register and its forward look: installations with inspection obligations and multi-year maintenance plans and budgets.

assets.name: Installation Record
assets.description: A technical installation or building element in the register of an object: central heating boiler or heat pump, lift, fire alarm and extinguishing systems, emergency lighting, legionella-relevant water installations, electrical installation, solar panels, entrance and access control, roof and facade elements: make, type and serial number, installation date and expected lifespan, location, contract and supplier, warranty, required periodic inspections and certificates with their legal basis (lift inspection under the Warenwet lift decree, gas boiler work under the CO certification scheme, fire safety under the Besluit bouwwerken leefomgeving, legionella management under the Drinkwaterbesluit, NEN 3140 electrical inspection, EPBD heating and cooling inspections), inspection history and next due dates, condition score and defects. Maintained in Installations and Periodic Maintenance (inst) on the object register, driving automatic supplier reminders and feeding Multi-Year Maintenance Planning and Budgets (mjop).
assets.businessMeaning: The compliance register of the building: an overdue lift or boiler inspection is a legal and safety liability for the owner, and the installation register is what turns reactive maintenance into planned maintenance.
assets.accessScope: technical staff of the owning tenant organisation; owner clients see the register and certificates of their objects; contracted suppliers see the installations they maintain; VvE boards see the association's communal installations

interfaces.name: installation register api
interfaces.description: Register, inspection schedule, certificate upload, condition update and due-date query API used by the technical module, work orders, maintenance planning, owner and supplier portals, the technical field app and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: installation compliance events
interfaces.description: Inspection due, supplier reminded, inspection completed, certificate expired and defect recorded events consumed by work orders, workflow reminders, owner notifications and planned-maintenance dashboards.

governance.retention: kept for the life of the installation plus 10 years with all inspection certificates, because building-safety and immovable-property records must be producible to authorities, insurers and buyers; superseded installations kept as history of the object
governance.sharingPolicy: shared with owner clients, VvE boards, contracted suppliers, insurers and inspecting authorities per object; transferred to the buyer on sale of the object; never shared between tenant organisations

assets.name: Maintenance Plan
assets.description: A multi-year maintenance plan (MJOP) and budget for an object, complex or owners' association: building elements and installations with condition scores from inspections (NEN 2767 methodology), planned maintenance and replacement activities per year over a 10 to 25-year horizon, cost estimates and indexation, capex versus opex classification, the reserve-fund contribution the plan implies for a VvE under the Wet verbetering functioneren VvE's, approval status by owner, board or meeting, and the realised work and cost per year against plan. Maintained in Multi-Year Maintenance Planning and Budgets (mjop) from the installation register, executed through Work Orders and Supplier Dispatch (work) and used by Association Budgets, Contributions and Reserve Funds (vveb) to size reserve funds.
assets.businessMeaning: The forward view of what the building will cost to keep: the basis of maintenance budgets, VvE reserve funds, capex planning and hold/sell analysis.
assets.accessScope: technical, asset management and VvE staff of the owning tenant organisation; owner clients and VvE boards see and approve plans for their objects; apartment owners see the approved plan of their association in the owner portal

interfaces.name: maintenance-plan api
interfaces.description: Plan, scenario, budget, approve, plan-versus-actual and reserve-fund calculation API used by the planning module, work orders, VvE budgets, owner portal approvals, dashboards and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: maintenance plan events
interfaces.description: Plan drafted, approved, activity due, activity executed and budget deviation events consumed by work-order creation, VvE budgeting, workflow tasks and planned-maintenance dashboards.

governance.retention: every approved plan version kept 7 years after the last year it budgeted, because VvE reserve-fund contributions and capex decisions are substantiated by it; superseded plans kept as history of the object
governance.sharingPolicy: shared with owner clients, VvE boards and members, lenders and buyers of the object; cost estimates never shared with suppliers before tendering; never shared between tenant organisations

rootGroups.name: Owners' Association Data
rootGroups.description: The Informant heritage: administration of owners' associations (VvE) as legal persons with their own budgets, contributions, reserve funds, meetings and decisions. Apartment owners are data subjects here and the association's books fall under the same fiscal retention as any Dutch legal person.

subGroups.name: VvE Administration
subGroups.description: The money and the governance of an association: budgets and contributions, and meetings and decisions.

assets.name: Association Budget and Contribution
assets.description: The financial administration of an owners' association (VvE) managed by a tenant organisation: annual budget per cost category approved by the members' meeting, the reserve fund with its statutory minimum (annual contribution of at least 0.5% of rebuild value or based on the MJOP under the Wet verbetering functioneren VvE's), the allocation key from the deed of division (breukdelen), periodic contributions per apartment right and owner with direct-debit mandates, arrears and collection status, extraordinary contributions for approved works, the association's own bank accounts and ledger, annual accounts and the owner statement at transfer of an apartment (notary request). Maintained in Association Budgets, Contributions and Reserve Funds (vveb) on the association's legal entity and billed through Rent Invoicing and Billing Runs (rent).
assets.businessMeaning: The association's financial health and the administrator's core deliverable: correct contributions, a lawful reserve fund and clean annual accounts approved by the members' meeting.
assets.accessScope: VvE administration staff of the owning tenant organisation; the association's board sees the full administration; each apartment owner sees its own contributions and the approved budget and accounts in the owner portal; notaries receive the statement at transfer

interfaces.name: association budget and contribution api
interfaces.description: Budget, allocation key, contribution run, reserve-fund, arrears and owner-statement API used by the VvE module, rent invoicing, dunning, the owner portal, notary statement requests and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: association finance events
interfaces.description: Budget approved, contribution run completed, contribution overdue, reserve fund below minimum and annual accounts approved events consumed by invoicing, dunning, owner notifications and association dashboards.

governance.retention: 7 years after the fiscal year under the bookkeeping duty of the association as a legal person (2:10 BW); the deed of division and allocation key for the life of the association; transferred to a successor administrator in full when the management contract ends
governance.sharingPolicy: shared with the association's board and members per their entitlement, its bank, accountant and the notary at transfer of an apartment; never shared between associations or tenant organisations

assets.name: Association Meeting Decision
assets.description: The governance record of an owners' association: annual and extraordinary members' meetings with convocation and notice period, agenda and documents, attendance and proxies, voting weights from the deed of division, quorum and majority rules per decision type, motions and voting results, minutes and approved decisions (budget, annual accounts, discharge of the board, maintenance works, house rules, appointment of the administrator), action items with owners, and the owner communication around them (notices, newsletters, digital voting). Maintained in Meetings, Decisions and Owner Communication (vvem) on the association's relations and served to owners through the Owner Portal (ownp).
assets.businessMeaning: The legal authority for everything the administrator does with the association's money and building: no contribution, work or budget is valid without the meeting's decision, and decisions bind future owners.
assets.accessScope: VvE administration staff of the owning tenant organisation and the association's board; members see convocations, documents, minutes and decisions of their own association and vote digitally through the owner portal; voting behaviour of individual owners visible only where the rules require it

interfaces.name: meeting and decision api
interfaces.description: Convene, publish documents, register attendance and proxies, vote, record decisions, publish minutes and track action items API used by the VvE module, owner portal, e-mail notices and workflow follow-up.

interfaces.name: meeting and decision events
interfaces.description: Meeting convened, documents published, vote closed, decision recorded, minutes approved and action item due events consumed by VvE budgets, work orders, owner notifications and workflow tasks.

governance.retention: minutes and decisions kept for the life of the association because decisions bind current and future owners; attendance and individual voting records kept 7 years; transferred in full to a successor administrator
governance.sharingPolicy: shared with the association's members and board; minutes provided to notaries and buyers of an apartment on request; never shared between associations or tenant organisations

rootGroups.name: Insight, Portal and Platform Data
rootGroups.description: The report and serve stages plus the foundation: governed analytics datasets behind dashboards, Power BI and investor reporting; portal accounts of tenants, owners and suppliers; the runs of automation robots and AI assistants; integration connections with their credentials; workflow tasks; and the tenant organisation that scopes every other asset to one real estate company with its licensed modules, entities and users.

subGroups.name: Analytics and Portals
subGroups.description: Derived data for steering and the accounts through which external stakeholders serve themselves.

assets.name: Analytics Dataset
assets.description: A governed, refreshed analytical dataset per tenant organisation: occupancy and vacancy, rent roll and rent growth, indexation effect, arrears and collection rates, service charge recovery, maintenance cost per unit and ticket resolution times, valuations and yields, project budget versus actual, VvE reserve positions, and the investor and owner reporting packs (NAV, income statement per entity and object, owner statements with recharges) built on them, with definitions, refresh timestamps, lineage to source assets and pseudonymisation of personal data. Built by Dashboards and Data Analytics (dash) from the object, contract, ledger and technical data, packaged by Investor and Owner Reporting (ivrp), served in the Owner Portal (ownp) and exposed to Power BI and other BI tools through certified connectors.
assets.businessMeaning: The cockpit of the real estate business: one set of agreed numbers that the director, asset manager, owner client and investor all look at, without a reporting project every quarter.
assets.accessScope: management, asset management and finance staff of the owning tenant organisation with report-level permissions; owner and investor clients see the packs and dashboards for their own objects and entities; BI connectors authorised per user role

interfaces.name: analytics and reporting api
interfaces.description: Dataset, KPI and report-pack query API with definitions and lineage, used by dashboards, investor and owner reporting, the owner portal and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: BI connector and report export
interfaces.description: Certified Power BI connector and OData-style feeds over the warehouse, scheduled Excel and PDF report-pack exports, and investor data-room deliveries.

interfaces.name: dataset refresh events
interfaces.description: Dataset refreshed, report pack published, KPI threshold breached and definition changed events consumed by dashboards, owner and investor notifications and workflow alerts.

governance.retention: datasets recalculated from source and kept as monthly snapshots for 7 years so that published investor and owner reports remain reproducible; personal data pseudonymised in the warehouse and never re-identified in reports
governance.sharingPolicy: shared with the tenant organisation's own users, its owner and investor clients per entitlement, and its BI tools under user authorisation; cross-tenant benchmarks only from anonymised, aggregated facts with tenant consent; never shared between tenant organisations otherwise

assets.name: Portal Account
assets.description: The self-service account of an external stakeholder of a tenant organisation: a tenant, apartment owner, owner client, investor contact or supplier user, linked to its relation and to the units, contracts, objects or work orders it may see: login identity (e-mail, verified phone, password hash or social or federated login), multi-factor authentication enrolment, consent and notification preferences, app device registrations and push tokens, branded portal of the tenant organisation, roles and entitlements, invitation and activation status, login and security audit trail, and data-subject requests raised. Identity and credentials are managed by Identity, Tenants and Access (iden); the account's profile, entitlements and preferences are served through the Tenant Portal and App (tenp), Owner Portal (ownp) and Supplier and Partner Portal (sprp).
assets.businessMeaning: The key to self-service: every rent payment, fault report, statement download, approval and work-order acceptance done through a portal account is handling time the organisation does not spend, and every account is a security boundary into tenant and financial data.
assets.accessScope: the account holder for its own account; portal administrators of the tenant organisation for invitation, entitlement and deactivation; platform operator support under logged access; credentials never readable

interfaces.name: portal account api
interfaces.description: Invite, activate, authenticate with MFA, manage entitlements, preferences and devices, and deactivate API used by the tenant, owner and supplier portals and apps, the back-office relation module and the identity service.

interfaces.name: portal account events
interfaces.description: Account invited, activated, login failed repeatedly, MFA enrolled, entitlement changed, consent changed and account deactivated events consumed by portals, security monitoring, relation records and self-service adoption dashboards.

governance.retention: kept while the underlying relation has an active contract, ownership or supplier role; deleted 90 days after deactivation; login and security audit logs kept 12 months; push tokens removed on device logout
governance.sharingPolicy: visible to the account holder and the tenant organisation's portal administrators only; federated login providers receive only what authentication requires; never shared between tenant organisations even when the same person deals with several

subGroups.name: Automation, Integration and Tenant Foundation
subGroups.description: The runs of robots and AI assistants, the connections to external systems, the tasks that route work to people, and the tenant organisation at the root of it all.

assets.name: Automation Job Run
assets.description: The execution record of a hyper-automation robot or AI assistant task for a tenant organisation: job type (bank reconciliation matching, rent run, indexation letters, dunning cycle, supplier invoice recognition and coding, ticket triage, document drafting, inbox classification, migration batch), schedule or trigger, input scope, model or rule version, steps and decisions taken with confidence scores, records created or changed, exceptions handed to a human with the reason, human review outcome, duration and cost, and an explainability trace that meets the EU AI Act transparency expectations for AI-assisted decisions affecting tenants. Produced by Hyper Automation and Robots (auto) and AI Assistants (aiag), with documents drafted into Documents and Correspondence (docm) and exceptions raised through Workflow, Tasks and Notifications (wflw).
assets.businessMeaning: The audit trail of work no human did: the proof behind the 100% time saving on repetitive financial processes, and the control that lets finance trust a robot with its books.
assets.accessScope: automation administrators and the finance, letting or technical staff of the owning tenant organisation who review exceptions; platform operator automation team for run health under logged access; never visible to external stakeholders

interfaces.name: automation job api
interfaces.description: Schedule, trigger, monitor, review exceptions, approve or reject robot decisions and replay API used by the automation console, AI assistants, workflow tasks, migration tooling and platform operations.

interfaces.name: job run events
interfaces.description: Job started, completed, failed, exception raised and human decision recorded events consumed by workflow tasks, operational dashboards, automation-rate KPIs and platform alerting.

governance.retention: run records and explainability traces kept 24 months for review and model improvement; runs that posted financial records keep their trace 7 years alongside those records; prompts and inputs containing personal data masked in logs
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the tenant organisation and the platform operator's automation team; AI model providers process data only under EU-hosted processor agreements without training on tenant data; never shared between tenant organisations

assets.name: Integration Connection
assets.description: A configured connection between a tenant organisation's platform environment and an external system: bank account-information and payment initiation under PSD2 through a licensed provider (consent tokens renewed every 180 days), accounting or consolidation packages, Power BI and other BI tools, e-signing provider, Gmail and Microsoft Outlook mailboxes, listing portals and the Huurprijscheck.app rent-price check, maintenance-partner platforms such as Ziezodan and Proprli, payment service provider, and third-party or customer applications on the open REST API and API Platform add-on: connection type and partner, scope and entitlements, OAuth tokens, API keys and certificates held in the secrets vault, webhook subscriptions, field mappings, sync schedules, rate limits, health and last-sync status, error log and the audit trail of who authorised it. Managed by Open API and Certified Integrations (apip) and scoped to the tenant organisation by Identity, Tenants and Access (iden).
assets.businessMeaning: The plumbing that makes the ERP the centre of the organisation's tool landscape: every credential here is a door into bank, mailbox or accounting data, and every broken sync is a silent gap in the books.
assets.accessScope: integration administrators of the owning tenant organisation; platform integration team for health and support under logged access; secrets write-only after creation and never displayed; partner developers see only their own API credentials

interfaces.name: integration management api
interfaces.description: Register, authorise (OAuth and PSD2 consent flows), configure mappings and schedules, subscribe webhooks, test, pause and revoke API used by the integration console, the API Platform developer portal, bank and accounting connectors and platform operations.

interfaces.name: integration health events
interfaces.description: Connection authorised, consent expiring, sync completed, sync failed, rate limit hit, credential rotated and connection revoked events consumed by workflow alerts, the bank and accounting modules and platform monitoring.

governance.retention: kept while the connection is active; revoked connections and their audit trail kept 24 months; secrets destroyed immediately on revocation; PSD2 consent records kept as required by the account-information provider agreement
governance.sharingPolicy: visible only to the tenant organisation's integration administrators and the platform operator's integration team; credentials never leave the secrets vault; partner systems receive only the tenant-scoped data their entitlements allow; never shared between tenant organisations

assets.name: Workflow Task
assets.description: A unit of work routed to a person or team inside a tenant organisation or to an external stakeholder: type (approve supplier invoice, review indexation proposal, handle ticket, follow up arrears, approve listing, sign contract, complete migration checklist, review robot exception), subject reference (contract, invoice, ticket, work order, meeting, job run), assignee or role, owner-client approval where the management mandate requires it, priority, due date and SLA, checklist state, comments, notification and reminder history across e-mail, portal and app push, escalation path and completion outcome. Managed by Workflow, Tasks and Notifications (wflw) and created by every module, robot and portal interaction.
assets.businessMeaning: Where the process actually lives: tasks make deadlines, four-eyes approvals and escalations explicit and measurable, so that indexation dates, settlement terms and inspection due dates are met without spreadsheets.
assets.accessScope: the assignee and its team within the owning tenant organisation; external stakeholders see only tasks addressed to them in their portal; managers see team task queues and SLA reporting

interfaces.name: workflow task api
interfaces.description: Create, assign, approve, comment, escalate, complete and query API for tasks and SLA states, used by every back-office module, the portals and apps, robots and AI assistants, e-mail and push notification delivery and the open REST API.

interfaces.name: task lifecycle events
interfaces.description: Task created, assigned, due soon, overdue, escalated and completed events consumed by notifications, portals, module status updates and throughput and SLA dashboards.

governance.retention: completed tasks kept 24 months for process analysis; approval tasks that substantiate financial decisions kept 7 years with the records they approved; notification logs kept 12 months
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the tenant organisation; tasks addressed to a tenant, owner or supplier shared only with that stakeholder; never shared between tenant organisations

assets.name: Tenant Organization
assets.description: The real estate company as a tenant of the platform: legal entity and contract with the platform operator, subscription with licensed modules (Relations, Projects, Objects, Technical, Contracts, Financial, Reporting, Portals), add-ons (portals, API Platform, VvE suite, projects, hyper automation), portfolio size bands for billing, brands and portal styling, document templates and letter texts, fiscal and localisation settings (country, language, VAT regime, invoice sequences, indexation defaults), users with roles and permissions, single sign-on configuration, administrative audit logs, migration state for organisations coming from Informant or other legacy systems, and the support and implementation history. Maintained by Identity, Tenants and Access (iden), onboarded through Data Migration and Onboarding Tooling (migr) and served by the customer success and implementation team.
assets.businessMeaning: The boundary of trust in a multi-tenant real estate ERP: every object, contract, invoice and ticket belongs to exactly one tenant organisation, and its licensed modules, users and settings decide what its people, robots and partners can do.
assets.accessScope: tenant administrators for their own organisation; platform operator support, implementation and tenant administration back office under logged access; API credentials visible only at creation

interfaces.name: tenant and identity api
interfaces.description: Tenant provisioning, module licensing, brand and template configuration, user and role management, authentication and single sign-on, and API-credential API used by all web applications, portals and apps, the open REST API gateway, migration tooling and the tenant administration back office.

interfaces.name: tenant and access events
interfaces.description: Tenant created, module licensed, migration milestone reached, user invited, role changed, credential rotated and tenant suspended events consumed by every module's authorisation cache, integration routing, portals and platform usage reporting.

governance.retention: subscription period plus 7 years for contract and billing records; user accounts deleted 90 days after deactivation; administrative audit logs kept 24 months; on off-boarding all tenant data exported in open formats and deleted within 90 days, with fiscal records handed over to the organisation before deletion
governance.sharingPolicy: visible only to the tenant organisation's own administrators and the platform operator's support and implementation staff; tenant identifiers passed to integration partners only to route calls; never shared between tenant organisations

stores.name: Portfolio Master DB
stores.description: Multi-tenant relational schema (PostgreSQL-style, row-level tenant keys) for legal entities, portfolios, objects, complexes, rental units, WWS point calculations, valuations, market data series and project budgets.

stores.name: Relation and CRM DB
stores.description: Relational store for contact relations, their roles, bank mandates, consent records, linked objects and contracts, document metadata projections and portal-account links; access-logged.

stores.name: Real Estate Document Store
stores.description: Object storage for signed contracts with e-signature evidence, deeds, energy labels, inspection certificates, appraisal reports, invoice PDFs, supplier invoice images, settlement statements, meeting minutes, photos and drawings, versioned and retention-classed per document.

stores.name: Correspondence Archive
stores.description: Archive of e-mails synchronised from Gmail and Microsoft Outlook, generated letters, portal messages and VvE notices threaded to relations, objects, contracts, tickets and meetings.

stores.name: Portfolio and Document Search Index
stores.description: Full-text and faceted search index over objects, units, relations, contracts, documents and listings used by back-office search, portal search and listing feeds.

stores.name: Letting DB
stores.description: Relational store for vacancy listings, viewing schedules, listing-channel publications, rent-price check results, application rankings and allocation decisions (with candidate details held in the screening vault).

stores.name: Candidate Screening Vault
stores.description: Encrypted, access-logged store for candidate applications, income evidence, masked identification and Wwft checks with purpose tags and scheduled purging after allocation.

stores.name: Lease Contract DB
stores.description: Relational store for lease contracts, rent components, indexation history, special terms, deposits, terminations, service charge cost pools, allocation keys, meter readings and settlements; contract versions immutable once signed.

stores.name: E-Signing Provider Mirror
stores.description: Synchronised copy of signature envelopes, signer events, timestamps and eIDAS evidence packages exchanged with the e-signing provider, keyed by envelope id.

stores.name: Real Estate Ledger DB
stores.description: Core multi-tenant, multi-entity financial store (PostgreSQL-style) for rent invoices, contributions, payment transactions, bank statement lines, supplier invoices, approval states, general ledger entries, VAT positions, period-close and consolidation state; append-only for posted entries and access-logged.

stores.name: Bank Statement Landing Zone
stores.description: Secure, immutable landing zone for CAMT.053 and MT940 statement files, PSD2 account-information pulls and manual uploads per entity bank account, with duplicate and gap detection before line ingestion.

stores.name: Bank Connector Mirror
stores.description: Synchronised copy of PSD2 account balances and transactions from the licensed account-information provider, SEPA direct debit batch statuses and R-transactions, and payment-service-provider payment records; holds no card data.

stores.name: Accounting Package Mirror
stores.description: Per-tenant staging and reconciliation copy of entities, debtors, creditors, journals and payment runs exchanged with external accounting or consolidation packages through certified connectors, plus XAF audit-file exports.

stores.name: Technical Management DB
stores.description: Relational store for maintenance tickets, work orders, quotes, completion reports, installation registers, inspection schedules and certificates, condition scores and multi-year maintenance plans with plan-versus-actual.

stores.name: VvE Administration DB
stores.description: Relational store for owners' associations: apartment rights and allocation keys, budgets, contributions and reserve funds, meetings, attendance, proxies, votes, decisions, minutes and action items.

stores.name: Real Estate Data Warehouse
stores.description: Per-tenant analytical warehouse behind the dashboards, investor and owner reporting and BI connectors, holding governed copies of objects, units, contracts, invoices, payments, ledger, valuations, tickets, work orders, projects and VvE finances with monthly snapshots; pseudonymised where source assets carry personal data.

stores.name: Analytics Export Store
stores.description: Serving store for Power BI connector datasets, OData-style feeds, scheduled Excel and PDF report packs and investor data-room deliveries, generated from the warehouse under user authorisation.

stores.name: Tenant, Identity and Portal Account DB
stores.description: Tenant organisation, subscription, module licence, brand, user, role, portal account, MFA enrolment, device registration, credential and administrative and security audit-log store backing platform-wide authentication and authorisation.

stores.name: Automation Job Store
stores.description: Document store for robot and AI assistant job runs with steps, decisions, confidence scores, exceptions, human review outcomes and masked explainability traces.

stores.name: Integration Configuration DB
stores.description: Relational store for integration connections, partner and API Platform registrations, scopes, field mappings, sync schedules, webhook subscriptions, health status and error logs; secrets referenced by vault id only.

stores.name: Integration Secrets Vault
stores.description: Hardware-backed secrets store for OAuth tokens, PSD2 consent tokens, API keys, certificates and signing keys of integration connections and API Platform clients; write-only after creation, rotated and access-audited.

stores.name: Workflow Task DB
stores.description: Relational store for workflow tasks, assignments, approvals, checklists, SLA timers, comments, escalations and notification delivery logs.

stores.name: Domain Event Bus
stores.description: Platform-wide, tenant-scoped event bus carrying contract, invoice, payment, ticket, work order, account, task and job events to portals, robots, workflow, integration webhooks, the warehouse and monitoring.
